That is the first PRD goal (inspect merge eligibility without risking a merge) and nothing beyond it; no history or query capability is added, which the PRD excludes. Reusing the existing floor reads keeps the merge-floor logic as the single source of truth, so the second goal is respected. The PRDR is warranted. Note for the DoD: the test should also assert the dry-run decision matches the real path's decision for the same inputs, so the two cannot drift apart.
